People going into that country will travel either by wagon or by boat. Ii they travel by boat they will not go by way of this road at all. They will go down the Athabasca river and then up the Peace river. If they are going by wagon they will go across country from the Athabasca river and then down the Peace river. If they are going by wagon they will get nearer to the mountains than the road which the hon. minister outlines here. I know what I am speaking about and I am satisfied that if the hon. minister consults any person who travels in that part of the country and who is familiar with the conditions there, he will find that the statement which I make is borne out. From Athabasca river at Fort Assini-boine, he can get a very , good road through a good country to Peace river and then if he wants to branch down to the lower Peace he can go down by water or by the road. The first road known as the Edmonton Trail was not built in a good locality.

I thought that all these expenditures in the Northwest were made through the Northwest Council. I think they have usually built these roads and that we have voted the money. Is it not intended to use this money in fhe same way ? Are we commencing to build roads independent of the Northwest Council ?

In a general sense that is the case, but in this particular case I am advised by the Department of the Interior that the object of the construction of these roads is to reach fertile districts and to enable settlers to get through. These districts are very sparsely settled at the present time and the Department of the Interior have recommended that it is in the interest of the Dominion in order to enable them to open up these lands that the Dominion shall make these small expenditures.
That is not the part that I am questioning at all. My question is : How will the money be spent ?
The money will be spent by this department.
Will it not be spent by the Northwest Council ?
No, it will be spent by the department.
We are to commence spending money that heretofore has been spent through the Northwest Council ?
In this case.
This is a departure from the policy which the government have followed for some years back ?

I have stated that this is an exceptional case. This vote is put in at the request of the Department of the In-

terior. There are certain Dominion lands which are valuable, and for the purpose of enabling settlers to reach these lands it is necessary to construct these roads. Our information is that the settlers are going in at a very rapid rate, but the country is very sparsely settled at present. In so far as this vote is concerned we are departing to that extent from the general policy of allowing the roads to be built by the Council of the Northwest Territories. The lands are .Dominion lands and the Northwest Council do not care to assume these particular expenditures. This government consider it to be in the interest of the country that these roads ^hould he built so as to open up lands which are owned by the Dominion.

It seems to me that as far as Manitoba is concerned the hon. minister has made the explanation very nicely. It is a rather unusual departure on the part of the government to commence building colonization roads in a province such as Manitoba and I think the government are establishing a dangerous precedent when they begin colonization roads through an organized province. The information that has been given to me is that in three cases each one of these amounts is to be expended in a way that is going to be a benefit to the candidates of the government who are now in the field.
In the absence of my colleague the hon. Minister of the Interior (Mr. Sifton) I am going to ask that the matter stand.

The information I have is that there is a certain foreign vote in the localities which are to be traversed by these roads and that the object of spending the money is for the reason 1 have given. It is a most extraordinary departure to undertake to spend the money of this government in that way and we ask that if you are going to spend money spend it in some proper way.
Give it to the Manitoba government.

Give it to the Manitoba government and give it to the territorial government. If yon spend it there, why should you not be called upon to do the same thing in every part of Manitoba, or in Ontario, or in any part of Canada ? I do not know any person who could have placed it before the House in a nicer way, hut it does not alter the case as I have stated it to the committee.
I do not view this item with very much favour and I do not believe that the people of the organized provinces of this Dominion will look upon it with very much favour.
We know well enough what they are doing it for.

We know what the idea is, hut we know it is a thing that should not be encouraged. We have organized provinces in the Dominion who look after then-roads and bridges ; and we pay a sum of money to the government of the Northwest Territories to administer the Northwest Territories. If they want $25,000 for building roads, this government should let them expend that as they expend the other money voted to them, if this system is allowed, tlie government will not hear the last of it. Our sessions are long enough now, hut if matters of this kind are introduced they will be extended. I am anxious to close the session, blit I will stay here to prevent this kind of thing. If this money goes to the Northwest Territories' government I have no objection.
So far as the Territories are concerned, this is not a precedent, because money was voted for this very road by this parliament five or six years ago.
Which road ?
One of the roads mentioned by the minister.

Athabasca river to Slave lake.
Mr. SPRuULE. Who spent the money 1
1 think the money was put in the hands of the Northwest Public Works Department.
Yes.
And the vote was made in this way. There is nothing to prevent the system being followed.

We have voted money every year for this purpose, and the vote was introduced by the Minister of the Interior, but the money went to the Northwest assembly and the work done under their control, hut now we are taking it out of their control.
'Mr. HYMAN. I simply asked the vote to stand in the absence of the Minister of the Interior. I said the department had no policy in the matter.
You said the Public Works Department was going to expend it.
I think you will find In ' Hansard ' that I merely said I presumed so.
I will apologize if the minister did not say that his department would expend this money.

I did not intend to say so, and I think you will find that I did not make the statement. There will be a full explanation if you allow the item to stand until the Minister of the Interior, at whose request it was introduced, is here.

When 1 asked if that were the policy of the government the minister said that it was a departure from their former policy, and that the Pubjic Works Department would expend it, but now he says the government have no policy.
I think it is a departure, because you do not find every year items of this kind.

I am speaking of the Territories.
I was speaking in reference to the whole item.
When the item comes up again would the minister let us know where that road runs from North Erwood, and- why they are building a road there ?
